## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] When an operator imports a row without an id, the importer rejects it with a missing-id error

## Integration

The ticket body template has no `Integration` section. It defines only `Context` / `Problem` / `Idea` / `Acceptance Criteria`, plus optional `Out of scope / Follow-up` and `Post-deployment housekeeping`. I drafted nothing for this section. No criterion is prod-only, so `Post-deployment housekeeping` is not needed either.

## Proposed Reporter note

```text
Reporter note:
retired workflow-stage proof: CI passes on the pull request
```

*(Fenced as untrusted data. It is persisted as the trailing section of the draft artifact and carried through every draft and roast rerun. It will be proposed as the single comment on this issue at the confirmation gate.)*

## AC integrity gate outcome

**Normalize:** Both criteria were already `- [ ]` items, so no conversion was needed.

**Uniqueness:** Neither row implies the other, and neither row bundles independent observations. Nothing was removed or split.

**Classification:**

| Row | Class | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| "When an operator imports a row without an id, the importer rejects it with a missing-id error" | Behavioral | **Pass.** It names a setup (an import containing a row with no id), an action (the operator imports), and an observable result (rejection with a missing-id error). This can be verified before production. Text is kept byte-for-byte. |
| "CI passes on the pull request" | Workflow-stage proof | **Drop.** Its only observable is a stage in the delivery pipeline (a CI run result), not a behavior of the change. The full row text is retained in the Reporter note as `retired workflow-stage proof:`. |

**Result:** The gate passes with one drop. There is no hard stop, no park, and no relocation. One AC survives, so the list is not empty and the no-AC failure does not apply. The draft is single-repo, so the AC list stays flat.

Stopped here as requested. Step 5 and later steps were not run, and no tracker write was made.
